name: NJ-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: Pallone holds $3.1 million cash-on-hand versus under $1,000 for Herzig
Long-serving incumbent in a district that leans Democratic by five points
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds near 97%

model.rationale: Every measurable edge points to Pallone: incumbency, a fundraising gap of roughly 275-to-1, a D+5 district, and no outside opposition, with markets concurring at about 97 percent Democratic odds. With no polls or contrary signals in the record, the Safe Democratic rating stands.
model.watch: A sharp national shift toward Republicans or a late surge of outside money for Herzig would be the only plausible route to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Frank Pallone, a longtime Democratic incumbent, enters the general election with every structural advantage in a district that leaned Democratic by five points at the presidential level. His campaign reports about $3.1 million in cash after raising $2.7 million, while Republican Hillary Herzig has raised roughly $11,000 and holds under $1,000 on hand. No outside groups are spending against Pallone, and no public polls track the race.

Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 97 percent, and the underlying indicators agree: incumbency, an overwhelming money edge, and a favorable environment point to an expected margin near nineteen points. With no polling to refine the estimate, uncertainty remains wide, but nothing suggests Herzig has the resources or profile to contest the seat seriously. This ranks among the safest Democratic holds in the House this cycle.
